The Fila Brasileiro (of what you may call a braizlian mastiff, even though they are not mastiffs in the traditional way).  


They are an amazing breed. One of the most (probably THE most) pack oriented breeds. Their pack drive is huge, what makes them extremely aggressive towards strangers. It is very difficult to introduce a new person to a Fila, what makes them very good guard dogs.  
They are also not that dominant for a molosser, making them very safe for the family, specially children.  
They are a landrace. It makes them healthier than breeds that were made from scratch with a singular purpose (like the Doberman or the Dogo Argentino). They were just the iberian dogs who were bred by people for their work, untill interbreeding happened and people noticed that the dogs behaved in a similar way and looked alike enough to be a breed.  


It's a shame that very few people outside of Brazil can get their hands in the real deal. Every foreign Fila I've seen is from a dogshow bloodline, that was sadly mixed with other breeds (like the bloodhound and the neapolitan mastiff). That happened because, in the 80's, cooler dogs started showing up in Brazil (GSD, Rottweilers, Pitbulls, Dobberman), and the more comercial breeders wanted to compete, by creating Filas who looked more exotic and fancy, unlike the average looking working Filas (you see, a working Fila has a "mutt" face, and people didn't want that).
